title: Wet the panel and keep the adhesive clean
text: Wet the fender before bringing the film over. Handle the film from an edge that will wrap under the hood where possible, and keep the adhesive away from fingers, clothing and the tire. The headlight is already out on the car shown, which gives access around its opening.
quality: A speck on your hand can end up under the film. Watch the loose sheet as well as the area you are holding; letting it touch the tire means stopping to deal with contamination.
alt: Wetting the dark blue Porsche 997 front fender before fitting paint protection film

title: Position the film before locking an edge
text: Lay the wet film over the fender and check its position against the panel edges. Keep enough control that it cannot slide into the tire. On this 997 pattern, the installer starts at the rear edge; that starting point is specific to the pattern and panel shown.
quality: Check the whole piece before committing to the first anchor. Correct alignment leaves material where the pattern needs it, without relying on extra stretch later.
alt: Positioning clear PPF over the Porsche 997 front fender

title: Anchor the rear edge and work out the solution
text: Secure the initial edge, then work away from it with controlled squeegee passes. Check where the film edge sits as you go. Use a clean cloth to see through the surface moisture before locking down the next area.
quality: Move solution toward an open edge. A pass that looks smooth while wet can still hide contamination or a trapped pocket; wipe and inspect before moving on.
alt: Anchoring the rear section of the Porsche 997 fender film

title: Lift only enough film to remove contamination
text: If you find a speck, stop. Lift the section you can access and clean, introduce application solution and work it around the end of the wet line. In the video, the installer chooses an accessible side of the pattern rather than peeling back the whole fender.
quality: Keep the clean adhesive protected. Forcing solution into an already bonded area can leave a visible adhesive line. Recheck the cleaned section before pressing it down.
alt: Lifting a section of PPF to clean beneath the Porsche fender film

title: Break a large finger into smaller sections
text: When a raised channel, or “finger,” forms, start farther back and work it into smaller channels with controlled passes. Leave a route for the water to escape, then close each smaller section in turn.
quality: Do not seal all sides of a pocket and leave the solution trapped inside. The installer also points out an existing paint scratch: inspect the paint first so you can distinguish old damage from an installation problem.
alt: Squeegee work around a raised channel in the Porsche 997 paint protection film

title: Dry the surface and inspect the edges
text: Wipe the surface with a clean microfiber cloth and inspect the actual film edge. Check for remaining fluid, raised areas and streaks. The demonstration leaves material beyond the edge for later finishing rather than pulling on wet film to force the fit.
quality: An edge that looks settled through a wet surface may still need attention. Inspect it dry and from more than one angle before deciding it is finished.
alt: Inspecting PPF fit along the Porsche front fender edge

title: Finish the edge after it has settled
text: Work back along the edge to press down remaining pockets and check adhesion. The installer waits until the edge is drier before final trimming so the film is less likely to lift. Follow the film maker’s instructions for any edge preparation product and keep it off incompatible surfaces.
quality: Finishing is an inspection step, not just a final pass with the tool. Check the entire edge, avoid unnecessary tension and arrange a follow-up inspection if an edge changes as the film settles.
alt: Finishing clear paint protection film around the Porsche 997 fender
